lines.text: 50,000 people are watching the highest-rated guy in the city fall apart.
And for the first time in his life, they can see the one number he's been paying to hide.
Let me back up.
In this world, everyone has ratings floating above their heads.
Strength. Athleticism. Health. IQ. EQ. Mental health.
They update live. Go for a run, your athleticism goes up. Skip a night of sleep, your health goes down.
Say something cruel, and everyone watches your EQ drop.
And everything runs on them. The café is hiring: EQ 70 and up.
The gym is members only: strength 80 plus. The bank only lends to an 80 overall.
And there's one rule everybody follows: you never date anyone more than ten points away from your own number.
This is Theo. Overall 52. Strength 41. Athleticism 47. IQ 104. EQ 93.
In this city, that's painfully average.
At the very bottom of his card there's a small grey number. Potential: 99.
Nobody reads the small grey number. Not even Theo.
Theo is in love with Mia. Overall 88. IQ 131. EQ 96.
That's a 36-point gap. In this city, that's not a crush. That's a joke.
The thing is, the day they met, Theo wasn't okay. His mental health had been sinking for weeks. 61. 52. 44.
Thousands of people walked past that number. They could all see it. Nobody said a word.
Mia was the first one who stopped. She sat down next to him and asked, "Are you okay?" And then she stayed.
Every time she laughed at one of his terrible jokes, his mental health went up by one.
But when two people look at each other, one more number appears. Compatibility.
Theo and Mia: zero percent. And standing right behind her is the guy she's 97% compatible with.
Kai. Overall 94. Strength 97. Athleticism 98. Two-time champion.
He won't shake hands with anyone under 80. His EQ is 19. And one line on his card is completely blank.
Because if you're rich enough, you can pay to hide one number. Kai pays 9,999 a month.
Every year the city holds The Ranking. Three rounds, live on TV.
The winner's card turns gold, and gold outranks every number.
So Theo signs up. The clerk reads his 52 out loud, and the whole stadium laughs.
Round one, the race. Kai wins without breaking a sweat. Theo comes in dead last. By a lot.
Round two, the puzzle. And something strange happens. Theo's IQ starts climbing, live on the giant screen. 104. 105. 106.
Second place. For the first time all day, nobody's laughing.
Then the final is announced. Partners are random, and every hidden number gets switched off.
The screen spins. Theo's partner? Kai.
The filters drop. Every card in the stadium flickers. And Kai's blank line lights up.
Mental health: 12. It's been 12 for years. That's what he was paying to hide.
The final is a wall. Halfway up, Kai looks down at 50,000 people reading his number.
9. 6. 4. He freezes. He can't go up. He can't go down.
Theo could climb right past him and win. Instead, he climbs back down.
He doesn't pull him. He doesn't push him. He just talks to him.
"Don't look at them. Look at the next hold. I'm not going anywhere."
And the whole stadium watches the number come back. 10. 25. 40.
Hold by hold, they climb together. They cross the line dead last.
Then the judges reveal how the final was scored. Not by time. By how much your ratings changed.
Kai's EQ jumped 40 points in one afternoon. Theo's? Every single stat went up.
His card turns gold. And for the first time, 50,000 people read the small grey number. Potential: 99.
That night, Mia walks right past the 97 and stands next to the zero.
Because compatibility only measures how alike two people are. They were nothing alike. That was the point.
Oh, and Kai? He cancelled his privacy plan. His mental health is right there on his card for everyone to see. It's 71 now.
50 years later, Theo and Mia are still on the same bench, still holding hands.
Compatibility: still zero percent. Mental health: both 100.
And every time she laughs, it still tries to go up by one.
So, if you could hide one rating, which one would it be? Tell me in the comments.
